title: MeetingHostRpc
description: The internal surface of tilo-connectors that tilo-api calls (FR-MTG-09, ADR-0032 decision 2 and addendum 1; FR-CON-02, ADR-0035 decision 2): what tilo-api posts to /internal/meeting-host/send, /internal/meeting-host/status, /internal/meeting-host/disconnect, /internal/connections/views, /internal/connections/start, /internal/connections/callback, /internal/connections/disconnect and /internal/side-effects/execute, and what each answers. Each route validates its own request and answer ($defs send_request and send_answer; user_request and status_answer; user_request and disconnect_answer; user_request and views_answer; start_request and start_answer; callback_request and callback_answer; connection_disconnect_request and connection_disconnect_answer; execute_request and execute_answer; error for any refusal) in both services; this root is any one of them. Every object is closed, and no field holds an access or refresh token, the client secret, a PKCE verifier, key material or a Meet link (ADR-0024 decision 4, ADR-0032 decision 3). Two fields carry a credential on purpose and nothing else does: callback_request.state and .code, the one-time values Google handed the browser (ADR-0035 LC-03; useless without the verifier and the client secret, which stay in tilo-connectors), and start_answer.authorize_url, the public part of the sign-in link. Ids travel in the body, never in a path or query. A route refuses a body over 65536 bytes (64 KiB) before it parses it. Rules that compare values (HB-03 the draft against its hash and the entry, HB-05 the owner, HB-07 the receipt against the entry, HB-09 the views against config/connectors.yaml, LC-05 the flow's person against the caller, LC-07 the items against the entry) are checked by the routes and by tilo-api's client, not by this schema. 1.1.0 adds views_answer, connection_view and scope; 1.2.0 adds the four live-connector routes' defs and the error codes start_again, not_granted and wrong_account (additive). 1.3.0 adds the three model-key routes of ADR-0041 decision 2 (Proposed and inert until config/byok.yaml enabled is true): /internal/model-keys/put, /internal/model-keys/remove and /internal/model-keys/status with the defs model_key_put_request and model_key_put_answer, model_key_remove_request and model_key_remove_answer, model_key_status_request and model_key_status_answer, and the error code key_refused (additive). model_key_put_request.key is the one more credential on this surface (BK-02): it is no-store and, like state and code above, nothing logs, stores or echoes it. /internal/model-keys/generate is model_call_rpc.schema.json's.

send_request.description: POST /internal/meeting-host/send, called only by the host run's outbox stub in tilo-api (HB-02). entry is the outbox entry (outbox.schema.json) tilo-api's outbox enqueued, evidence the case its enqueue checked, and draft the pinned item the owner approved. It names no user: the grant used is (entry.authz.ref, meeting_host). The then branch narrows entry to the one action this surface runs (MH-10), a meeting invitation the owner approved: state queued, create_meeting_event on meeting_host, T3 with the new_recipients modifier, 1 to 50 recipients (MAX_RECIPIENTS), no attachments, the draft pinned as item, the host account's primary calendar as destination, no undo window, authorised by a person. (The narrowing sits in if/then so the generated type stays Outbox.)

evidence.description: The OB-01/OB-05 case tilo-api's own enqueue checked (outbox.rules.md), without the entry: reserved_by is the gate's approval.requested event and authorised_by the approval.resolved event that answered it (event.schema.json, each with its data schema applied in the then branch, so the generated type stays Event), world_owner is the world's owner. A meeting invitation is T3, so no policy, Team Lead, instruction or earlier policy.applied takes part: those are null or empty. tilo-connectors runs the same check on its own outbox (HB-04) and trusts these copies (ADR-0032, residual trust).

draft.description: The pinned draft the owner approved (kind meeting_event): the bytes tilo-api read from the run's artifact store, hash-checked there (AR-01), because tilo-connectors cannot read that store. HB-03: the SHA-256 of the decoded bytes equals content_sha256, artifact_id and version equal entry.item, and the document parses as kind meeting_event. content_b64 is padded base64 (RFC 4648 section 4) of at most 43692 characters, the base64 of 32 KiB, so a request with 50 recipients stays under the 64 KiB body cap. The same shape is one entry of execute_request.items (LC-07), where the document is the entry's item or attachment and the body cap bounds the sum.

send_answer.description: The 200 answer to send. sent: the invitation exists at Google and receipt says what was made; tilo-api checks it (HB-07) before storing it. refused: nothing was sent and nothing will be (SideEffectRefused, HB-03 to HB-06). possibly_sent: Google may hold the invitation and a retry would not help (PossiblySent). retry: try again later; may_have_sent is false when nothing reached Google (not connected, expired, a missing scope, a KMS outage) and true after a Google 5xx or a lost answer. receipt is set only with sent and may_have_sent only with retry; otherwise each is null. parts lists what the broker emitted during the call; tilo-connectors writes no data.transfer and raises no alert of its own outbox here, because tilo-api's outbox does (one writer per world).

receipt.description: What the adapter made (HostReceipt): Google's event id, never a link. HB-07: event_ref equals side_effect_marker(entry); world_id, outbox_id and draft equal the entry's; meeting_id and owner equal the draft's. tilo-api stores it through the run's receipt store only when all hold.

draft_ref.description: The draft the receipt was made from, by id and version only (no label).

user_request.description: POST /internal/meeting-host/status, POST /internal/meeting-host/disconnect and POST /internal/connections/views. user_id is the signed-in principal's own id in tilo-api, never one taken from a body, path or query there (HB-02, HB-08); the bot account's meeting_host grant is (user_id, meeting_host), and views reads only this user's grants.

status_answer.description: The 200 answer to status: a store read only, with no token use and no Google call, so it emits nothing and has no parts. state is connected, expired (Google refused the grant; connect again) or none (no grant stored); scope_ok is true when the stored grant holds the calendar.events.owned scope, and false when there is none.

disconnect_answer.description: The 200 answer to disconnect. revoked_at_provider is true only when Google confirmed the revoke. The call is idempotent: with nothing stored it answers false with no parts. parts carries connection.revoked, and an alert.raised for each revoke kept for a retry.

views_answer.description: The 200 answer to POST /internal/connections/views (ADR-0032 addendum 1, HB-08, HB-09): the connection views of the request's user_id, one per stored grant of a connector that config/connectors.yaml declares with auth oauth2, in registry order, each connector at most once. A connector with no stored grant is absent (tilo-api shows it available); a disconnect deletes the grant, so it is absent too. A store read only, with no token use, no KMS call, no provider call and no event, so it has no parts. At most 32 views. tilo-api treats an answer that breaks this contract or HB-09 as unknown as a whole, never as partly read.

connection_view.description: One stored grant of the request's user, from an allowlist: connector, state, scopes and connected_at, nothing else of the record. state is connected when the stored state is exactly connected, else expired (Google refused the grant at refresh, or a record the broker did not write: connect again). scopes are the stored granted scopes that the registry declares for this connector, sorted and unique, and none when expired. connected_at is when the grant was made (HB-06), null when expired or not recorded; it is display data read without KMS and authorises nothing. Never a token, the record's ciphertext, wrapped key or nonce, the client id or secret, the access token's expiry or an account address.

scope.description: An OAuth scope as config/connectors.yaml declares it: a URL or a word from a closed alphabet, at most 300 characters, with no query, fragment, user info, percent sign or space. A backstop only: HB-09 sends only scopes the registry declares for the view's connector.

parts.description: What the broker emitted during one call, in order, nothing more (ADR-0032 decision 7): tilo-api hands each connection part to meeting_host.on_connection_event. Every connection part names the call's own user (entry.authz.ref for a send, the request's user_id otherwise); a part naming anyone else is not that call's, and tilo-api's client drops it. At most 16.

connection_part.description: A connection event of the meeting_host grant: expired (Google refused the grant at refresh), rate_limited, or revoked (a disconnect). Type, connector and user only.

alert_part.description: An alert.raised the broker emitted (a revoke kept for a retry): its alert id only.

start_request.description: POST /internal/connections/start (ADR-0035 decision 2, LC-06): begin the person's Google sign-in for one connector. user_id is the signed-in principal's own id in tilo-api, never one taken from a body, path or query there (HB-02). The route asks Google only for the declared scopes of these capabilities minus those already granted, with include_granted_scopes. A connector that is not an oauth2 connector of the registry, or a capability it does not declare, is invalid_request (the route checks the registry, not this schema). meeting_host uses the same route for the bot account.

start_answer.description: The 200 answer to start. authorize_url is the Google sign-in link the web opens: the accounts.google.com authorisation endpoint with a percent-encoded query (client id, redirect URI, the asked scopes, the PKCE challenge, state; no secret) of at most 2048 characters, or null when no scope is missing, in which case no flow was made (LC-06). The PKCE verifier and the client secret stay in tilo-connectors (LC-03); the pattern is a closed shape and a backstop that refuses a query naming a secret.

callback_request.description: POST /internal/connections/callback (ADR-0035 decision 3, LC-05): the browser came back from Google. user_id is the signed-in principal's own id in tilo-api (HB-02). state and code are the one-time values Google handed the browser and the only place this surface carries them (LC-03): the code is useless without the verifier and the client secret, and tilo-api never logs, stores or echoes either. Exactly one of code (the person agreed) and error (Google's own lower-case error word, for example access_denied, when the person did not; the route never echoes it) is present, absent and never null. The route spends the state on first use and refuses unless the flow's user equals user_id (LC-05).

callback_answer.description: The 200 answer to callback: the connection was stored. connector is the one the flow was for. scope_lines are the plain-language lines of what Google granted, one per text, in the order asked (a partial grant lists only what was granted; none granted is the not_granted error, so there is at least one). parts lists what the broker emitted during the call (connection.established); it carries no token and never a connection.consented, which is the person's Connect on a consent card and tilo-api writes it (CR-13).

connection_disconnect_request.description: POST /internal/connections/disconnect (ADR-0035 decision 2): the person disconnects one connector. user_id is the signed-in principal's own id in tilo-api (HB-02). Google keeps one grant per client for a person (CON-D10), so disconnecting any person connector revokes the shared grant and every connector resting on it ends; the web says so before the person confirms.

connection_disconnect_answer.description: The 200 answer to /internal/connections/disconnect: disconnect_answer with the parts of any connector. revoked_at_provider is true only when Google confirmed the revoke; the call is idempotent (with nothing stored it answers false with no parts). parts carries a connection.revoked for each connector that ended, and an alert.raised for each revoke kept for a retry.

execute_request.description: POST /internal/side-effects/execute (ADR-0035 decision 5, LC-07), called only by a live connector's outbox stub in tilo-api (HB-02). entry is the outbox entry tilo-api's outbox enqueued, evidence the case its enqueue checked and items the pinned content, hash-checked in tilo-api (AR-01) because tilo-connectors cannot read that store: the entry's item first, then each attachment in the entry's order (HB-03: the hashes, ids and versions equal the entry's). The grant used is the world owner's (evidence.world_owner). The route re-runs the same check on its own outbox (HB-04) and refuses an action its connector does not declare with a gate. The then branch narrows entry to the live Google connectors (gmail, google_drive or google_calendar; meeting_host has its own route, lovable no call at all): state queued, or scheduled with its undo window spent (OB-02), a pinned item, at most 10 attachments. The caps do not add up to 64 KiB: the body cap bounds the sum, and a request over it is invalid_request before anything acts. (The narrowing sits in if/then so the generated type stays Outbox.)

execute_evidence.description: The OB-01/OB-05 case tilo-api's own enqueue checked (outbox.rules.md), without the entry, for a live Google connector's side effect (evidence is the meeting host's, narrowed to its always-T3 case). reserved_by is the gate's approval.requested event, null when a policy opened the entry. authorised_by is the approval.resolved that answered approve or the policy.applied that opened it, never null (an entry exists only once authorised). world_owner is the world's owner. policy is the record policy.applied names, or the one a Team Lead answered under; team_lead that Team Lead's record; instruction the whole event policy.applied.instruction_id names (L2); each null when it does not apply. earlier_applied is the owner's earlier policy.applied events (the day's count and an instruction's single use), at most 50, [] on a gate path. Each event has its data schema applied in the then branch, so the generated type stays Event. tilo-connectors runs the same check on its own outbox (HB-04) and trusts these copies (ADR-0032, residual trust).

execute_answer.description: The 200 answer to execute, as send_answer with result for receipt. sent: the effect exists at Google and result says which; tilo-api stores it only when result.marker equals side_effect_marker(entry) (LC-08). refused: nothing was done and nothing will be (SideEffectRefused: an item hash, the entry check, a grant missing or newer than the approval, an action the connector does not declare, an event with guests under create_event, LC-09). possibly_sent: Google may hold the effect and a retry would not help. retry: try again later; may_have_sent is false when nothing reached Google (not connected, expired, a missing scope, a KMS outage) and true after a Google 5xx or a lost answer. result is set only with sent and may_have_sent only with retry; otherwise each is null. parts lists what the broker emitted during the call; tilo-connectors writes no data.transfer and raises no alert of its own outbox here, because tilo-api's outbox does (one writer per world).

execute_result.description: What the adapter made, by Google's own id and Tilo's marker only, never a link, a title, a subject or mail text. resource_id is the Gmail message or draft id, the Drive file id or the Calendar event id (letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, at most 256, the adapters' own RESOURCE_ID). marker is side_effect_marker(entry), 32 lower-case hex characters, the same on every retry and instance (OB-03).

connector_parts.description: What the broker emitted during one call of a connect, disconnect or execute route, in order, nothing more (ADR-0032 decision 7, ADR-0035 decision 2): as parts, but a connection part may name any connector and may be connection.established. Every connection part names the call's own user (the request's user_id; evidence.world_owner for an execute); a part naming anyone else is not that call's, and tilo-api's client drops it. At most 16.

connector_part.description: A connection event of a grant: established (a connect stored it), expired (Google refused the grant at refresh), rate_limited, or revoked (a disconnect). Type, connector and user only. connection.requested and connection.consented are never parts: they belong to the consent card (CR-13) and tilo-api writes them.

model_key_put_request.description: POST /internal/model-keys/put (ADR-0041 decision 2, BK-01 to BK-03): store the org's key as a new version of its Secret Manager secret, then validate it with the provider's free list-models call from tilo-connectors, to the profile's pinned host, with no redirect and a 3 second limit (BK-19). org_id is the verified principal's org in tilo-api, never a browser value (BK-08); the secret's name comes from org_id and slot, never from the body. key has the shape of the owner's PUT body and is the one credential on this request; the body is no-store.

model_key_put_answer.description: The 200 answer to put: the new secret version and whether the provider accepted the key. validated false means the version was created disabled because the process may not go live (EFF-01): the status is unverified and no run can use it. A key the provider refuses is the error key_refused and no version is kept. A rotation disables every earlier version only once the new one validated (decision 2).

model_key_remove_request.description: POST /internal/model-keys/remove: with secret_version, destroy that one version and re-enable the one it displaced (the compensating act when tilo-api's reference write failed after put, so the old key stays active); without it, destroy every version and delete the secret (the owner's removal). Idempotent. Nothing is ever left enabled after a rotation or a removal (BK-01).

model_key_remove_answer.description: The 200 answer to remove: true when a version or the secret existed and is gone, false when there was nothing to remove (still a 200).

model_key_status_request.description: POST /internal/model-keys/status: a store read only, with no secret access, no provider call and no event.

model_key_status_answer.description: The 200 answer to status, about the org's latest version: none (no version), active (enabled and validated), unverified (created disabled, never validated) or disabled (a rotation, three refusals or a failed re-validation disabled it, BK-17). secret_version is null exactly when state is none. No key character, length or hash.

error.description: The body of every refusal on this surface, a fixed code and nothing else: unauthenticated (401, no valid ID token, HB-01), forbidden (403, any account but tilo-api's, HB-01), invalid_request (422, a body over 64 KiB, not JSON or not this contract's request; refused before anything acted) and not_configured (503, a setting is missing or a seam failed to build, or LIVE is not set on tilo-connectors; also 502 when Google's certificates cannot be had to check the token, which is retryable and never a final 401). Only /internal/connections/callback adds three, each 400: start_again (the state is unknown, spent, expired, another person's or lost with an instance, or Google did not accept the code, or the grant could not be saved; one text for all, so the answer says nothing about which, LC-05), not_granted (the person did not agree, or none of the access asked for was granted) and wrong_account (meeting_host only: the sign-in was a person's own account, not the bot's, MH-C1). Only /internal/model-keys/put adds one, 422: key_refused (the provider refused the key; no version was kept, ADR-0041 decision 2). Never a value, a setting's value or an exception's text.
